title: Goldman Sachs Sees India Growing 7.2% in 2027, Well Ahead of China's 4.5%
excerpt: Goldman Sachs Research forecasts global growth of 2.8% in 2027 on rising AI investment and easing oil prices, with India's 7.2% forecast above the 6.8% consensus — and risks tilted to the downside.
body:
• Goldman Sachs forecasts India's economy will grow 7.2% in 2027, ahead of China's 4.5% and above the 6.8% consensus estimate for India.
  • Global growth is forecast at 2.8% in 2027, marginally above the estimated 2.7% in 2026 — "solid but unremarkable," in chief economist Jan Hatzius's words.
  • The outlook leans on AI investment rising to $1.8 trillion in 2027 from $1.1 trillion in 2026, and Brent crude easing to $78 a barrel by the end of 2027.
  • These are forecasts, not results: Goldman says risks are tilted to the downside, including an escalation of the Iran conflict and weaker AI spending.

Goldman Sachs expects India's economy to grow 7.2% in 2027, outpacing China's projected 4.5%, even as global growth stays modest at 2.8%, according to the bank's latest Global Economic Outlook from Goldman Sachs Research.

The India forecast is a moderation from the bank's estimated 7.9% growth for 2026, but it sits above the consensus estimate of 6.8%. China's projected 4.5% is slightly ahead of its 4.4% consensus forecast, with exports expected to help offset weak domestic consumption and continued stress in the property sector, IANS reported.

"We expect another year of solid but unremarkable GDP growth in 2027."

— Jan Hatzius, Chief Economist and Head of Goldman Sachs Research

What is driving the forecast

Goldman Sachs expects global GDP to rise 2.8% in 2027, marginally higher than the estimated 2.7% expansion in 2026, as lower energy prices and continued investment in artificial intelligence offset tighter financial conditions and reduced fiscal support. Hatzius said the outlook reflected shifting drivers of activity, with energy costs, technology spending and fiscal policy doing more of the work than in earlier cycles.

The bank's commodity strategists forecast Brent crude falling to $78 per barrel by the end of 2027, alongside a similar moderation in liquefied natural gas prices. On technology, nominal global AI investment is projected to rise to $1.8 trillion in 2027 from $1.1 trillion in 2026, led largely by US hardware spending, which the bank sees rising by more than $500 billion. It estimates AI investment will add 0.4 percentage points to global GDP growth next year. The bank also expects the United States to grow 2.4% in 2027, up from 2.3% in 2026, and US core PCE inflation to fall to 2.4% by the end of 2027 from 3.2% at the end of 2026.

Risks and what to watch

Goldman Sachs warned that risks to the outlook remain tilted to the downside. Hatzius cited a possible escalation in the Iran conflict, wider fiscal deficits and weaker-than-expected AI investment as threats, along with constraints on AI infrastructure, regulatory uncertainty and credit market stress. The bank also expects the pace of AI investment growth to slow after the first half of 2027, and sees further monetary tightening in some major economies early next year before room for rate cuts opens as inflation slows.

For investors, the report frames 2027 as a year in which India retains a clear growth premium over China inside a low-growth world economy. The figures are Goldman Sachs forecasts, and the bank's own caution is that the drivers behind them — energy prices and AI spending — are also its main downside risks.
